kind: independent review of completed functional resume traces, not a new execution

notIncluded: full independent audit of every functional assertion

verdict: Desktop Hall and Sphere preserve a real two-second audio-advance assertion failure: sampled AudioContext.currentTime and output timestamp are flat while JS observers and engine.onTick continue. Separate obsolete quality assertions are additional failures, not substitutes for the audio failure. Mobile-emulated cases pass their short resume checks under different settings/sample rates. Root cause and audio quality are unproven.

cases.method: Real UI, keyboard and CDP touch input; captured main rAF with explicit complete WebGL frames. Functional assertions only; no FPS or performance claim.
fixtures: Fresh browser context, deterministic Math.random seed 417, initial manual quality and audience enabled in localStorage.
Google Fonts requests use explicit local font files from FONT_ROOT; external font connectivity is outside this check.
The app main rAF is captured; other rAF callbacks, the UI and audio clock remain native. Each requested main frame really renders and readPixels completes its WebGL work.

Listener assertions compare the intended target pose. A baseline without the target cache records the original setListener inputs after calling it unchanged; interpolated AudioParam values are not treated as immediate targets.

Seat reachability: director.placeAt places the walker beside a real unoccupied seat, avoiding a long venue walk. Seat selection itself uses E or the touch sit button; standing uses E or the real walk button.
After the real sit input, director.update(2.5) finishes only the existing camera tween; the seated frame still renders normally.

Before the real 공연 시작 click, snapRoster places only the current score track/chair roster and snapConductor completes its conductor entrance. This avoids pending exits of unrelated players while main rAF is captured; the real runConcert waits, audio start and controls remain active.

observed: The two desktop traces keep audioState running and document visible, with no statechange/visibilitychange event recorded.
After the resume click, each desktop trace has 22 samples, audio/current output timestamp constant, and onTick +81 over approximately 2.01 seconds.
Identical audioNow values already occur in show-started, paused and before-resume snapshots. The point where clock progress ceased cannot be assigned to the resume click.
Later explicit frames show audioNow progressing after other controls/rendering. These are not repeats of the same resume condition.
Hall mobile and Sphere mobile cross the original threshold in about 308ms and 344ms Node-observed diagnostic windows.
notEstablished: The root cause is not isolated to the product, browser audio implementation, software graphics/readback interaction, or audio output environment.
onTick progress establishes observed JavaScript callback progress, not audio graph rendering or physical sample delivery.
A 100ms observer is not an audio callback profiler and cannot measure output dropouts, skipped notes, late scheduling, exact A/V sync or sound quality.
Desktop/mobile are not a controlled A/B: initial quality, audience, sample rate, viewport and some collector checks differ.
These captured-main-rAF tests do not establish simultaneous native rendering and music stability, sustainable FPS, physical mobile behavior, heat or battery life.
interpretation.followUpBoundary: Keep all original failures. Assess any updated-collector retry, baseline/candidate native-rAF comparison and physical-device/output checks as separate artifacts; none is marked PASS here.

qualityExpectationAnalysis.hallDesktop: Snapshot 4583ac3 expects min(DPR,1.25)=1 for medium; product main at dea defines min(DPR,1.25)*0.85, observed 0.85. This explains the second assertion mismatch, not the earlier audio timeout.
qualityExpectationAnalysis.sphereDesktop: Snapshot 983c1a0 fixes manual preset DPR but still expects returning to auto to equal initial manual high. Product capability path identifies software renderers as a medium initial tier; the raw automatic-setting frame reports medium. This explains the separate second mismatch; actual GL renderer identity is not independently captured here.

audioSourceComparison.interpretation: Whole engine/performance files differ. The inspected diff changes listener/spatial target caching and crowd preparation in engine.js, and visual chair updates in performance.js. No play/pause/seek/note scheduling hunk is in this diff; that is a static observation, not proof that surrounding changes or environment cannot affect runtime.

derivationProcedure: Require closed wrapper metadata and matching raw/summary status and collector hash.
Compare stdout SHA and transferred/runtime bytes against original completed files.
Locate the first sample whose cause is after-resume-click; derive deltas/min/max/unique counts through the final sample.
Compare show-started, paused and before-resume snapshots without assuming where the freeze began.
Read exact collector snapshots for original assertions and trace instrumentation; preserve two independent desktop failures.
Compare the 12 served source hashes with git show at the declared commit, and inspect audio source diff only for scope.
Rehash all consumed artifacts; write only this review.
